english.title: Wrongful disclosure of information about a prisoner
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person

(A)_[who was]_
(B)_[who had been]_

employed

(C)_[in pursuance of prisoner escort arrangements]_
(D)_[at a contracted out prison]_
(E)_[performing contracted out functions at a directly managed prison]_

disclosed otherwise than

(F)_[in the course of duty]_
(G)_[as authorised by the Secretary of State]_

information namely **(..SPECIFY INFORMATION..) which

(H)_[he]_
(I)_[she]_

acquired in the course of

(J)_[his]_
(K)_[her]_

employment and which related to a particular prisoner, namely **(..SPECIFY NAME OF PRISONER..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 91(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 1991.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Option E was added on 3.11.94 by section 100 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order 1994.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
